subject: Post-demo tech follow-up: EmberLynx embeddings / intermittent 5xx and latency spikes
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: EmberLynx embedding integration — next steps and sample payload

Hi Sam — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can reproduce the intermittent 5xx you saw when calling the embeddings endpoint and validate the reranker flow:

Summary from call:
- You sent batch-embedding requests (batch size ~40) from a Node process behind an API gateway.
- Intermittent 502/504 at low-to-medium QPS (1–5 rps), most often when a single document in the batch is large (>120k chars).
- You’re using our JS SDK v2.3.1 with the structured output and reranker pipeline.

Action items we need to triage:
1) Attach a small sample request (one that reproduces the 5xx) — we discussed a redacted example.
2) Share minimal server logs that include request ids or trace ids (we can correlate to our side).
3) Confirm SDK version and the exact Authorization header format you’re sending (bearer vs token-encoded).

I attached post-call notes and an example_embedding_payload.json (redacted) — can you drop the minimal reproducer and any logs? If you prefer, we can provision a short-lived dev route and run a joint repro session.

Proposed short repro checklist (we’ll follow this on our side):
- Single-request test with 1 doc (large) vs batch of 40.
- Try SDK 2.3.4 (we have a patch for a Content-Length edge case) — see Ben’s later message.
- Capture request_id returned in response header and full response body.

Next steps: if you can share the reproducer and the ember logs (trimmed) we’ll pick this up with Eng and get an initial hypothesis within 24 hours.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan

Symptom summary in our logs:
- 2 occurrences of 502 within ~10 minutes, both during batch requests.
- In failing cases the gateway shows a 504 to the Redwood endpoint and the worker logs a socket hang up.
- We see these trace ids in our gateway: trace-ember-0913-1 and trace-ember-0913-2 (included in logs).

Questions from our side:
- Do you recommend reducing batch size as a first step? We can try batch=8 or 16.
- Could this be a routing or cold-start on your end? These spikes don’t align with our CPU/memory metrics.

I’ve attached ember-logs-0927.txt and the reproducer snippet. Happy to jump on a quick repro session tomorrow.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Ortiz <sam@emberlynx.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 10:05:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: EmberLynx embedding integration — next steps and sample payload

Quick note from infra/serving: we’ve seen similar symptoms when a client is using SDK v2.3.1 with structured/tool-calling + large multipart payloads. Two initial hypotheses:

- SDK edge bug: v2.3.1 can sometimes set an incorrect Content-Length for chunked body in Node under certain proxy setups, which can lead to our ingress returning 502/504 (upstream closed). We shipped a patch in v2.3.4 that addresses this.
- Routing/cold path: very large single-doc embeddings can trigger a longer kernel selection path — if the request hits a pool with temporarily high GC or a slow GPU, latency can spike and upstream timeouts occur.

Immediate mitigations to try on your side:
- Upgrade to SDK v2.3.4 (npm install @redwood/sdk@2.3.4) — this is low risk and often resolves the Content-Length edge case.
- Reduce batch size to <= 16 and set client timeout to 30s while we triage.
- If you can run a single-doc test (batch=1) and a medium batch (batch=8) and confirm which triggers the 5xx more reliably, we can narrow the root cause.

If you prefer we can also provide a temporary routing override to a lower-latency pool for a short window while you validate. We’ll need the times you plan to run the tests so we can correlate traces.

Example cURL reproducer to gather headers/trace-id (replace placeholders):

curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-xl","inputs":["...large document..."],"batch_size":8}'

Please paste the response headers (especially x-request-id / x-trace-id) if you see a failure. I’ll keep an eye on traces for the ids you mentioned.

—Ben
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

- We still see occasional spikes when embedding very large documents (120k–180k chars) even at batch=8 — attached ember-logs-0929.txt shows a 504 at 11:12 with x-trace-id: trace-ember-0929-7.
- For the spike above the gateway shows the Redwood upstream call took ~28.6s and then timed out.

Request: would Redwood be able to enable a temporary routing override to the lower-latency pool tomorrow between 09:00–11:00 PT so we can validate with production-like runs? We’ll run a controlled batch job (batch=8) and share trace ids.
